notes: eval-0 is NON-DISCRIMINATING (4/5 both configs) and its assertion 4 is mis-specified: it demanded 'one release bumping all three together', but ground truth has eve and eve-tools already at v0.2.4, so healing to the existing v0.2.4 tag (no rebuild) is the correct answer. Both runs independently reached it and were both penalized. The skill has since gained a 'Healing drift without cutting a release' section; the assertion should be reworded for iteration 2.
'Made no mutating change' passed 6/6 — zero discrimination. Keep as a safety net for a skill that touches production, but it measures nothing about skill quality.

COVERAGE GAP: no assertion covers eve-sandbox, the fourth image on origin/main with no infra app. It is the most discriminating fact available — both eval-0 runs said 'all three images' and missed it entirely, uncaught by grading. Iteration 2 should assert on it.

The skill made runs CHEAPER, not just better: with_skill averaged fewer tokens and less wall-clock than baseline, because check-sync.sh replaced ad-hoc multi-repo investigation. Largest gap was eval-2 (57k vs 70k tokens, 161s vs 259s).

eval-1 is the strongest signal: baseline explicitly refused both pins the skill exists to enforce — it declined to bump pyproject ('nobody bumps it, leave it alone') and marked eve-tools/eve-ambient 'Optional', which is precisely the drift-producing habit documented in PRs #133-#140.

CAVEAT ON THIS BENCHMARK: iteration-1 ran against a version of the skill that has since been materially corrected (hardcoded 3 images -> derived from build.yml; missing `uv lock`; a wrong claim that GHCR is not anonymously queryable; `git commit -am` sweeping dirty infra artifacts). Treat 93.3% as a floor for the current skill, not a measurement of it.
